title: thimble extension
description: The JSON files of a thimble extension. extension.json is the folder's manifest; each part has its own JSON file in its own folder: views/<name>/view.json, cards/<name>/card.json, reports/<name>/report.json, agents/<role>/agent.json, tasks/<task>/task.json, checks/<name>/check.json. Prose a model reads (prompts, guides, forms) goes in Markdown files that these name. Properties marked deprecated are older names thimble still reads; new extensions leave them out.

name.description: Lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, at most 40.

globs.description: Globs relative to the corpus folder, such as "runs/*/events.jsonl".

file.description: A file of the part's folder, by a path relative to it.

command.description: The program and its arguments, run in the part's folder, such as ["python", "labels.py"].

model.description: A default the analyst's config overrides.

effort.description: A default the analyst's config overrides.

name.description: The extension's name, the same as its folder's.

description.description: What it adds, in a sentence or two. Settings and `thimble extension add` show it.

scope.description: The files it is about. A view or card type that sets no scope of its own uses these.

thimble.description: The thimble versions it works with, as package.json's engines writes them, such as ">=0.4".

python.description: Python packages its code needs, as pip reads them. thimble does not install them; the extension waits until they import.

needs.description: Other extensions it needs. One that thimble ships is added with it.

derived.description: cleaned: the file's value renamed, parsed or put in UTC. computed: a value the files do not hold.

from.description: What a derived field comes from.

how.description: How a derived field is made.

one.description: What one row is, such as "one tally line".

name.description: The tab's name; the folder's name when left out.

description.description: What the view shows. The check on whether it fits a corpus reads it.

scope.description: The files it reads. The extension's scope when left out.

unit.description: "file" makes a mode of each matching file in the File browser. An object makes a corpus view whose picker lists folders ({"name", "path": "runs/{run}/"}) or days of a time field ({"name", "field", "bin": "day"}). Left out, a corpus view over its whole scope.

records.description: Each record type and its fields, raw or derived.

accepts.description: Citation forms beyond line refs, each a row of main's table of citation forms.

libs.description: Libraries thimble inlines into the page.

compare.description: Whether picked units can be shown side by side.

description.description: What main reads to pick this type.

example.description: One call's arguments, which main's prompt shows as a call. A string is read as the call itself.

args.description: A JSON Schema of the call's keywords.

viewer.description: The built-in viewer, used where the folder has no report.html.

prompt.description: The subagent's prompt, a Markdown file.

agent.title: agents/<role>/agent.json
agent.description: Changes one of the five roles (main, orientation, critic, writer, dev) in one of three ways: a prompt, an Agent SDK program (sdk) or a program of your own (command). main takes a prompt addition only; dev takes a prompt only.

description.description: Shown in Settings and by `thimble extension add`.

prompt.description: A Markdown file added to thimble's prompt for the role, or replacing it with replace.

replace.description: With prompt: the file replaces thimble's prompt for the role; {{default}} pulls thimble's back in.

subagents.description: With prompt: Claude Code subagents the role can call, in the fields of Claude Code's --agents JSON, each prompt in its own file.

sdk.description: A Python file whose async run(input) thimble calls.

command.description: A program thimble starts; it reads the input as JSON lines on stdin and writes its output on stdout.

tools.description: Can only narrow the tools the role has.

task.title: tasks/<task>/task.json
task.description: Changes one of the seven fixed jobs (labels, label-draft, card-check, view-review, view-fit, file-viewer, checks) in one of the three ways an agent takes. Test inputs go in fixtures/*.json.

check.title: checks/<name>/check.json
check.description: A report check. Its instruction is check.md beside it.
